chapter: The union and the 1920s-30s band scene
title: The original Club Alabama on Spring Street
summary: The band moved from Vernon to Mike Lyman's Club Alabama on Spring, whose name the Central Avenue Alabam later took; Fanchon and Marco staged revues there, and the clientele is debated.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Is that where the Club Alabama was then?
That's --
On Spring Street?
Yes.
Yeah.
You see, the Alabama on Central had taken the name from the Alabama on Spring.
Oh, I didn't know about the other one. You didn't tell me about that.
I didn't know that. Which year was that?
Oh, that was in -- I believe that was in '26, if I'm not mistaken.
So that was the original Club Alabama. On Spring Street.
Yeah.
And that's where you were, too?
Oh, yeah, we worked there.
Yeah, I didn't know about that one.
I had everybody.
Well, tell us who. You remember some
of the names who worked there?
Yeah.
See, I always thought Central was the only Club Alabama in Los Angeles.
Oh, no.
No, huh? Well, who were some of the people, do you remember?
In the band?
Yeah, at the Club Alabama on Spring.
Same bands.
Same bands.
Same band, yeah, same people.
Now, were there mixed audiences at the time, black and white, coming in the club?
Oh, yeah.
No, it wasn't a mixed clientele. They could have, but they didn't.
Well, was it mainly all white or mainly black at the time, that would come in to hear you?
No, I -- Susie said no, but I seen white and black in there.

Well, they could come, but I don't remember seeing any colored. They could come, but those that did come, they come upstairs and sat on the balcony and talked and chatted with us, just (inaudible). See, and then when it
closed there, that's when the band went to the Cotton Club
See, that Abe Lyman's brother on that Alabama on Spring Street.
What was his name?
Abe Lyman. He had a band, remember?
Oh, Abe Lyman and Mike Lyman were brothers.
Right.
Oh. How long --

And at the time, Fancheon of Fancheon and Marko staged the reviews there at the Alabama, because she was married to one of the Lyman Brothers. She was one of the sisters, and she married -- what was his name? Simon.
Simon.
But she was Abe -- Mike Lyman's sister-in-law.
Yeah, (unintelligible), yeah, sister-in-law.
You know the dance team? Fancheon and Marko?
Yeah. How long was there a Club Alabama downtown?
Oh, a long time.
And how long did you work there?
How long did we -- oh, about two or three years.
Two or three years?
No, not that long.
Not that long? She says not that long.
No. It was about -- I guess we worked there about six weeks.
At the Club Alabama?
Right.
The one downtown.
See, we left out of Vernon Country Club and went to Club Alabama on Spring Street. And then we went from there to the Cotton Club.
Okay.
Same thing comes to your mind. All we can do is use just little ideas here and there, yeah. It doesn't have to be a work of art.
